VERDICT
- Proceed. Replace the flat AGENTS.md + index concept with a 3-layer progressive-disclosure system (L0 routing index → L1 per-repo map → L2 on-demand module docs), hard token budgets, fixed schema, and explicit staleness tracking. This is the Stacker pattern worth imitating: agents load the smallest layer that answers the question.

REASONING
- AGENTS.md alone conflates routing with detail; a central index alone gives no edit confidence. Layering solves both: L0 answers "which repo," L1 answers "where in this repo and is it safe," L2 answers "how does this module work" only when needed.
- Single-file-per-unit satisfies the loadable constraint: one L0 index globally, one L1 map per repo. Agents never read more than one file to orient.
- Token efficiency comes from enforcement, not intent. Without budgets (~500 tok L0, ~1.5k L1), maps bloat into the full-repo read you were avoiding.
- Hand-maintained maps rot; fully generated maps are noise. Semi-automated scaffold (tree + git log + entry-point grep) plus curated annotations is the maintainable middle.
- Staleness kills trust. A map without a `last_verified` date gets ignored by agents after one bad experience, and the whole system dies.
- Cross-repo work (5 repos, likely shared ports/envs/data flows) needs an adjacency list at L0 or agents will miss dependencies when a task spans repos.
- Common failure modes to pre-empt: embedding code snippets (rot instantly), duplicating grep-able facts, describing aspirational instead of actual state, no acceptance test.

NEXT_STEPS
1. Define L1 schema (use verbatim for all 5 repos): `# MAP: <repo>` / `purpose:` (1 line) / `status: active|paused` + `last_verified: YYYY-MM-DD` / `entry_points:` (exact commands + files) / `tree:` (depth ≤3, annotated one-liners, `!` prefix = do-not-touch) / `key_files:` (path → why, ≤10 rows) / `state:` (active work, known-broken, WIP branches) / `relationships:` (consumes/produces, ports, shared env/creds, cross-repo deps) / `agent_start:` (numbered first actions, test command, what not to touch) / `deep_docs:` (pointers to L2, load only on demand).
2. Write the L0 index: one line per repo (purpose, status, map path) + adjacency block (`llm-bridge ↔ resolume-bridge: port X, shared .env key Y`) + routing rule ("edit KalshiML model code → read KalshiML/MAP.md first").
3. Scaffold generation script: `tree -L 3`, `git log --oneline -10`, grep for `main|app|index|serve` entry candidates → draft map per repo. Then manually annotate purpose/state/agent_start. Budget ~30 min per repo, starting with the most-edited one.
4. Enforce budgets: L0 <500 tokens, L1 <1.5k tokens, L2 optional and unbudgeted but never auto-loaded. Add token count as a comment at the top of each map.
5. Wire maintenance into workflow: agent definition-of-done includes "map touched files' sections updated; bump last_verified." Rule: if a session changes entry
